feed.title: NPR Topics: Climate
feed.subtitle: NPR's full coverage of climate change and related issues.

entry.title: Isaias pummels the Gulf Coast, and plows through Alabama
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias landed Friday night on the Florida Gulf Coast. The storm was expected to bring life-threatening storm surge, damaging winds, flooding and the possibility of tornados.

entry.title: Former NOAA official on coastal cities' vulnerabilities during severe weather
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep talks with former NOAA official Carolyn Gruber about vulnerabilities in the infrastructure of coastal cities during extreme weather events.

entry.title: Isaias strengthens into the first hurricane of the Atlantic season
entry.summary: Tropical Storm Isaias is now the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 — and it's spinning toward the southeastern U.S.

entry.title: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
entry.summary: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.

entry.title: Super El Niño is here. What's so super about it?
entry.summary: This year, federal forecasters say the planet could see the strongest El Niño event on record. Here's what you need to know.

entry.title: Studying this super El Niño could save lives. NOAA is scaling back research
entry.summary: A powerful El Niño is already influencing extreme weather around the planet. During the last strong El Niño, federal agencies ramped up research in the hope of improving weather forecasts. This year, they won't be matching that effort.

entry.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
entry.summary: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

entry.title: One year after the end of the EV tax credit, is the future still electric?
entry.summary: Congress got rid of a $7,500 federal tax credit for new electric vehicle buyers. One year later, are people still buying EVs?

entry.title: How low-cost climate solutions are helping cities recover from major storms faster
entry.summary: Cities like New York are bouncing back faster from major rainfall and flash flooding, thanks to smart, low-cost climate solutions.

entry.title: Hurricane Polo's remnants bringing more rain to flood-struck U.S. Southwest
entry.summary: The storm's remnants battered the U.S. Southwest, flooding roadways and forcing residents in small New Mexico towns to evacuate over concerns about a dam failing.
